Statement and Proof 1.1–4.1 remain blocked. The handle definition requires 0<=k<=m, but the Statement allows k>m and hence an undefined disk D^(m-k). More substantially, an immersive k-direction slice does not imply full m-rank: (x,y)->(x,0) has rank k<m. The disk supplier neither provides transverse derivatives nor proves the thickened-handle restriction/fibre equivalence. The LES supplier compares already established fibrations and cannot create those missing hypotheses or prove the component comparison automatically. Francis Lectures 5–6 Lemma 1.3 and Lecture 7 Lemmas 0.2/0.4 identify the genuine dimension-qualified fibration that is required but leave its full good-position argument unsupplied here. Attempted closure by treating D^(m-k) as a parameter fails that rank test. Owner/Step-5b must prove the dimension-matched thickened-handle family theorem, including the attaching-collar fibre and pi0 comparison, and clarify the relative smooth-neighbourhood premises; retain the replacement/withdrawal proposal and open risk review. OWNER RESOLUTION PROPOSAL: Full source rank is preserved by cocore local addition and triangular compression; the original full map is retained near Q, with O(v^2)/O(v) transition estimates. All handle indices obey 0<=k<=m and k<n. Statement and Proof 1.1–4.1 are false. Set X=point and N=R: interval immersions based at zero have nonzero derivative of constant positive or negative sign, hence at least two fibre components, represented by t and -t. Formal interval data also retain a nonzero interval-direction linear map. Ordinary paths in Imm(point,R)=R have no such derivative constraint; the exponential-law set bijection does not remove the interval direction from the source tangent bundle. Path shrinking at its terminal time gives zero interval derivative and leaves the immersion locus. Attempted closure by using path spaces is exactly this rank loss. The valid consumer prerequisite must instead compare extension over a collar of a fixed-dimensional boundary region or suitable germs. Francis Lectures 5–6 uses dimension-preserving restriction squares; neither it nor the reviewed smoothing supplier proves this false product reduction. Owner/Step-5b must authorize and prove a replacement interface; retain the proposed withdrawal and open risk review. OWNER RESOLUTION PROPOSAL: Dimension-preserving collared-domain compression preserves all tangent directions; no extra source interval is identified with an ordinary path parameter. Proof 1.1–6.1 does not establish the classical claim. Componentwise reduction requires a mapping-space product over source components, rather than the written map-into-disjoint-union argument. In Proof 2.1 a compact component W of M_0 is not generally open in ambient M; its boundary is nonempty because empty boundary would make W ambient clopen. L2 also calls the existing dual-elimination supplier not-yet-authored. The decisive gap is Proof 4.1: a compact parameter map into Imm(M,N) is a family defined on all M, not a map S^k->M with compact source image; restriction gives an inverse limit. Stagewise comparisons alone do not prove an ordinary limit comparison. Proof 5.1 asserts locally finite corrections without a compatible stationary-on-compacts construction or accumulated-time jet continuity, and invokes compact-source genuine smoothing for noncompact M. Its Statement lacks the smooth-near-Q premise present in Given and the actual smoothing supplier. Attempted closure using a handle schedule requires the unresolved genuine handle/collar prerequisites and compatible extension data. Sources consulted: Francis Lectures 3 and 5–6 and Lecture 7; they do not provide the promised completed countable-limit argument here. Owner/Step-5b must supply that relative exhaustion construction or a proved inverse-limit/fibration theorem and rebuild the invalid suppliers. The classical open-source theorem is not claimed false. Risk remains open. OWNER RESOLUTION PROPOSAL: The compact source induction uses subcritical handles and collar extension. Countable stages are eventually stationary on every compact source set. Endpoint columns use the same constant base collar; witnesses are smoothed before smooth source-dependent time substitution. Statement and Proof 1.1–3.1 remain blocked. Normal identifications are extra data: for M=point, N=R, the enriched space is R times GL1(R), with two components, while ordinary point formal data is R. Thus the declared subspace identification is ill-typed. A horizontal splitting of the total disk tangent sequence needs a connection or supplied split sequence, not just the base tangent-normal identity. The embedded-submanifold Euclidean normal-addition supplier does not by itself extend an arbitrary immersion into N. Contractible point fibres without a fibration do not imply weak equivalence (discrete-to-indiscrete identity on two points is a counterexample). The invoked product-collar theorem is false and does not compare a disk interior with its closure. Francis Lectures 5–6 Definition 1.8/Lemma 1.9 and the final comparison square (PDF pp.3–4) distinguish enriched normal data and use forgetful fibrations; its local extension sketch does not prove this written interface. Attempted closure by forgetting identifications fails already for a point. Owner/Step-5b must define enriched spaces properly and prove parametric germ/extension comparisons, a tangent splitting and forgetful-fibration LES descent, preserving relative data and AC_omega. The positive-rank disk-bundle preliminaries reviewed here do not supply those missing results. Keep the proposed rebuild and risk open. OWNER RESOLUTION PROPOSAL: Formal and genuine normal thickening comparisons are proved with fixed compact radius relative tests, tangent-normal transport and enriched-to-ordinary gauge descent, rather than identifying decorated normal data with an ordinary component.
